claim: Layang-Layang, Sabah Trough and Kinabalu Basin are three structural positions within one collision system (lower plate / foredeep / upper plate), not three independent basins.

One collision (COLLISION_MM), three opposite expressions: RU drowning without major erosion on the lower plate; foredeep onset in the trough; DRU uplift-erosion on the upper plate. They are physically different surfaces with different seismic signatures.
source: Arif ENTERPRISE relay + Clift et al. 2008 + Hinz 1985
confidence: MED-HIGH for order, LOW for exact age

claim: BANGKIT (PROPOSED, not adopted): a Late Miocene lithospheric-rebalancing event beneath Sabah drives post-16 Ma deformation independent of renewed plate collision. Evidence verified 2026-09-30: uplift/exhumation ~8–3 Ma at >7 mm/yr (Menier et al. 2017); Late-Miocene apatite+zircon cooling of the Crocker belt (JGS 2000 thermochronology); PSCS slab remnant beneath Sabah confirmed geophysically (Cornwell et al. 2025 JGR W-dipping discontinuity 45–55 km; Pilia et al. 2023; Yu et al. 2021; Shi et al. 2020). Mechanism OPEN (break-off vs delamination vs dripping vs crustal melting). Kinabalu granite INTRUSION age UNVERIFIED (K-Ar range to 14 Ma contested); BizChat's 9–7 Ma window is narrower than the evidence. SRU (9–8.5 Ma) sits at the onset edge — BANGKIT as SRU driver plausible, unproven.
source: BizChat enterprise analysis 2026-09-30 (names INVENTED, pending F13) + FI-003 source verification 2026-09-30 (search-snippet class; full texts not yet read)
